 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 04-02-2022.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 04.02.2022 at about 10.30 a.m. while petitioner was riding his motor cycle i.e.,
TVS Jupiter Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-07-EE-6997, in front of Gulpet Police Station, Kolar Town, Kolar, at that time, the driver of the TATA Sumo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-G-338 belongs to Police Department, came from opposite direction i.e., on wrong side of one way road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's motor cycle and as a result, petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.

Immediately, petitioner was shifted to R.L. Jalappa hospital, Kolar wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and spent amount of Rs.1,00,000/- for his treatment, medicine etc.,
3.
It is further stated that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as a Coolie and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work as doing earlier.
It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the TATA Sumo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-G-338.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the Owner and 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its learned counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and hence, he was placed exparte.
5. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It has denied the age,
income and occupation of the petitioner and the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner 2nd respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of TATA Sumo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-G-338 and contended that its liability is subject to the terms and Syed Nawaz Pasha vs Superintendent Of Police on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62470696/
2 conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: It is contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner himself, as he had not possessed valid and effective D.L. as on the date of accident.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues :-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 04.02.2022 at about 10.30 a.m. when he was proceeding by riding TVS Jupiter Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-07-EE-6997, at Kolar Town and when he reached in front of Gulpet police station, on Kolar - Chikkaballapur road, at Kolar Town and District, at that time, the driver of the TATA Sumo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-G-338 came from opposite direction and driven the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, lolst control over his vehicle and dashed against the vehicle in which the petitioner was proceeding, due to which he sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, from who and how much?
3. What order or award?
7.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and they got marked 13 documents as per Ex.P1 to 13.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not led its defence evidence.

8. Heard the arguments from both side and perused the materials available on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 ... Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 ...

As per final order  For the following:
 REASONS 10. Issues No.1: As per the case of the petitioner, on 04.02.2022 at about 10.30 a.m. while he was proceeding in the motor cycle i.e., TVS Jupiter Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-07-EE- 6997, in front of Gulpet Police Station, Kolar Town, Kolar, at that time, the driver of the TATA Sumo Car bearing Reg.No.KA- 07-G-338 belongs to Police Department, came from opposite direction i.e., on wrong side of one way road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against his motor cycle and as a Syed Nawaz Pasha vs Superintendent Of Police on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62470696/
3 result, he fell down and sustained injuries.

sentences.text:
The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, Spot Mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate and Charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to 6.
11.

According to the version of petitioner, the accident happened in front of Gulpet Police station,
Kolar Town, at that time, the driver of TATA Sumo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-G- 338 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 being the Spot Mahazar, conducted in the place of accident.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 it reflects that the injured was proceeding in a scooter bearing No. KA- 07-EE-6997, the rider of the Tata sumo Car bearing No.KA- 407-G-338 came from opposite side in a negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the petitioner's scooter.

As per this document accident occurred on one-way road, width of the road is 22 feet and offending vehicle came from opposite direction on one-way road, by violating the traffic rules, which makes it clear that, the driver of the Tata Sumo police vehicle, who is expected to enforce rules for the general public,
violated the traffic rules and, without observing the oncoming vehicle, dashed against the petitioner's scooter on the opposite side, towards the right side of the motor cycle.

If the rider of the Tata sumo driven it in a normal speed by observing traffic rules and on going vehicles on the road,
then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Further more, even the chargesheet as per Ex.P6 was also filed as against the driver of the Tata sumo police vehicle.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P3 and 4 coupled with Ex.P6 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata sumo police vehicle.
12. Even in the instant case the driver of the offending vehicle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part.

After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Tata sumo police vehicle bearing registration No.KA-07-G-338 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
There is no reason to take a different view.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-07-G-338.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of TATA Sumo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-G-338.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
14. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:

It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as a Coolie and earning Rs.30,000/- per month and to prove the same,
petitioner has not produced any documents.
In the absence of document to prove the actual income and avocation, the tribunal has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year 2022.

Therefore, by considering the Syed Nawaz Pasha vs Superintendent Of Police on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62470696/
4 avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- per month.

sentences.text: The petitioner claims that he is unable to work due to accidental injuries sustained by him.
The petitioner got examined Dr.Nagakumar, working as Professor in the Department of the Orthopaedics, at R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, as PW.2.
In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained injury to his right shoulder, left thigh, leg and foot.
On examination he found that healed surgical scar mark present over proximal to distal part of the right thigh on the lateral aspect.
Further, he assessed the disability of 45.6% to the left lower limb and that of to the whole body at 15% of the petitioner.
The doctor has produced disability evaluation form with calculation which is marked as Ex.P11.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
PW.2 is not a treated doctor and the disability assessed by him has to be taken into consideration carefully.
Hence, considering the nature of work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 10% disability to his whole body.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 24 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 04.02.2022.
However, by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P8 Adhaar card as 10.06.1999, the petitioner was aged 23 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 23 is 18 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

Hence, petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,34,800/-(Rs.15,500x12x10x18/100)
towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

15. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
As per wound certificate produced at Ex.P5, the petitioner has sustained a) Closed displaced comminuted fracture of Right femur, Shaft at Middle 1/3rd region,
b) Displaced fracture of distal phalanx of left hand middle finger,
c) Right Nasal bone fracture Syed Nawaz Pasha vs Superintendent Of Police on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62470696/
5 d) Multiple abrasion over face each 1x1 cms.
The doctor has opined that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

sentences.text: The Ex.P7 Discharge Summary of R.L. Jalappa Hospital reveals that petitioner took the treatment as an inpatient in the said hospital from 04.02.2022 to 05.02.2022 wherein he underwent ORIF+NAILING FOR RIGHT SHAFT OF FEMUR FRACTURE +ALLOGENOUS BONE GRAFTING +SS WIRING ON 5-2-2022 Under Spinal Anesthesia.

Again he took treatment as an inpatient in the said hospital from 02.09.2022 to 05.09.2022, at that time he underwent surgery for Bone Marrow injection at fracture site for uniting right femur shaft fracture at Middle third done on 03-09-2022 Under Spinal Anesthesia.

Therefore, by considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.50,000/-
towards pain and sufferings.
16. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.71,129/- at Ex.P9.
I have perused the medical bills and receipts.

Further the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.71,129/- and he is entitled for the same.
17. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:

As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 6 days, certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.6,000/- under this head.

18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least three months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.46,500/- (15,500X3) under this head.

19. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 23 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer the discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 10% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.30,000/- on this head.

20. Thus in all, the petitioner entitled for the compensation as here under:

21. Interest:
The petitioner is claiming interest @ 9% p.a. on the compensation amount.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
22. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle TATA Sumo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-G- 338.
The breach of any of the policy conditions are not proved.
It is not disputed that 2nd respondent is the insurer and 1st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, 1st respondent being the Owner and 2 nd respondent being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2 nd respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,38,429/- (Rupees Five lakhs thirty eight thousand four hundred and twenty nine only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount, 70% of the award amount shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 30% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 2 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
